packages.objective: Replace the inherited CC Switch runtime surface with a branded, least-authority 野菜API shell and implement the frozen five-tool local read-only discovery query and its beginner-facing result states.
deliverables: A minimal Tauri runtime that exposes only tool-discovery-scan@v1 to the RU-001 frontend and does not initialize inherited provider, database, network, updater, telemetry, credential, configuration, or installation services.

A bounded cross-platform scanner for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH with exact version display, canonical candidate deduplication, timeout handling, sanitized location classes, and conservative read-only compatibility.
A distinctive accessible 野菜API first screen covering default, loading, empty, partial, error, expired, conflict, recovery, and processing behavior with no unavailable product actions.
Executable acceptance evidence for catalog completeness, conservative compatibility, conflict handling, failure isolation, no-side-effect authority, and stale-request rejection.
nonGoals: No account login, device authorization, balance, usage, pricing, recharge, or NewAPI integration.
No API key, operating-system credential vault, model, line, configuration-file content, configuration write, backup, rollback, repair, or tool lifecycle action.
No automatic update, compatibility download, telemetry, crash upload, server, Nginx, DNS, database, or production change.
No claim that any detected tool version is approved for automatic configuration.

migrationPolicy.dataBackfill: RU-001 creates no application database, account record, configuration receipt, compatibility cache, or retained scan history.
migrationPolicy.rollback: Revert only the listed allowed paths to the upstream fork baseline; no user or server data migration or restoration is involved.

compatibilityPolicy.strategy: Consume the fixed tool-discovery-scan@v1 projection and fail closed: every successful version probe is unverified_read_only until a later frozen release unit introduces signed exact-version evidence.
compatibilityPolicy.supportedVersions: RU-001 discovers arbitrary installed version strings but supports zero versions for automatic configuration; the scanner command contract is tool-discovery-scan@v1 only.
compatibilityPolicy.removalGate: Changing the five-tool catalog, enabling a configuration action, adding a remote catalog, or changing status semantics requires a superseding accepted decision and a newly frozen release unit.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: When no executable exists, the result still contains each of the fixed five tools exactly once and every card truthfully reports not found without treating absence as an application error.
A successful version probe preserves the exact normalized version, reports the sanitized source class, and remains unverified read-only with no automatic-configuration action.
Two distinct canonical executable candidates produce a visible multiple-installation conflict and the scanner neither selects one nor grants compatibility.
A failed or timed-out version command affects only its own tool result, returns no raw command output, and does not prevent a complete five-tool projection.
The RU-001 runtime registers only the discovery command, has no network or updater permission, and the scanner source contains no configuration, credential, lifecycle, or filesystem-write authority.
If two scans overlap, completion of the older request cannot replace the newest request's visible state and the UI exposes a new explicit rescan action after recovery.

stopConditions: The frozen query or page-state contract is missing, contradictory, or requires a status not defined by tool-discovery-scan@v1.
A required implementation change falls outside allowedPaths or touches any forbidden path.
The implementation would need network, updater, telemetry, configuration content, credential, filesystem-write, tool installation, server, NewAPI, Nginx, DNS, database, or production authority.
A detected version would need to be presented as automatically configurable without a later verified exact-version allowlist.

packages.objective: Preserve RU-001 and add the honest beginner-facing account and billing shell plus the deterministic desktop-account-readiness@v1 projection, while updating the future NewAPI interface specification from current verified evidence.
deliverables: A coherent Account and Local tools navigation that preserves the frozen RU-001 discovery flow and introduces no unavailable live action.
A pure local desktop-account-readiness@v1 projection whose only RU-002 runtime status is backend_upgrade_required and whose remote facts remain unavailable.

A beginner-readable account composition for authorization, balance, today and month usage, model ID, official and actual pricing, fixed display-only FX context, and recharge, with no fabricated numeric result.
An updated NewAPI future-change specification pinned to current official GitHub and deployed read-only evidence, clearly distinguishing current routes from proposed desktop routes.
Executable acceptance evidence for fail-closed readiness, no network or secret authority, truthful placeholders, fixed FX semantics, RU-001 preservation, and server-spec provenance.
nonGoals: No real device authorization, website login, account query, balance, usage, model, pricing, wallet, payment, subscription, recharge, token, or API-key operation.
No password, website cookie, access token, refresh token, PAT, API key, account profile, price row, usage row, or wallet URL persistence.
No client-side interpretation of NewAPI billing_expr and no independent numeric official-price table.
No NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, production, updater, telemetry, configuration, credential-vault, third-party tool, or package lifecycle change.

migrationPolicy.dataBackfill: RU-002 creates no account, credential, billing, usage, price, authorization, wallet, cache, or retained readiness record.
migrationPolicy.rollback: Revert only the listed client shell, readiness projection, locale, acceptance, and narrative specification paths to RU-001; no user or server data migration or restoration is involved.

compatibilityPolicy.strategy: Preserve tool-discovery-scan@v1 unchanged and fail closed for every remote account or billing capability through desktop-account-readiness@v1.
compatibilityPolicy.supportedVersions: RU-002 supports the completed RU-001 discovery contract and supports zero deployed NewAPI versions for account integration because the required /api/desktop/v1 boundary has not been verified as deployed.
compatibilityPolicy.removalGate: Activating authorization, balance, usage, pricing, models, or recharge requires a superseding release unit with a new deployed integration contract, secure-storage evidence, and real contract tests.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: The local readiness projection has exactly one RU-002 status, backend_upgrade_required, marks every remote capability unavailable, reports networkAttempted false, and identifies only the future /api/desktop/v1 namespace.

The Account shell labels balance, today usage, month usage, model ID, official price, actual price, and recharge as unavailable or login-gated and contains no sample, zero, cached, or inferred account value.

RU-002 account-owned source performs no fetch, HTTP client, Tauri remote invocation, external open, storage write, cookie access, credential access, token handling, or secret-bearing URL construction.
The client displays exactly 1 USD = 6.75 CNY as a fixed display-only comparison context, explicitly not a live exchange rate or billing input, and displays no independent numeric model price.
The successor shell still invokes only scan_tools_read_only for the five-tool scan and preserves stale-request rejection, exact tool identities, and the absence of configuration actions.

The future NewAPI specification names current GitHub HEAD and deployed readiness evidence, marks /api/desktop/v1 paths as proposed and not deployed, and states that this unit changes no NewAPI or production resource.

stopConditions: A required client behavior would need a real account, pricing, usage, authorization, wallet, payment, token, credential, or network operation.
A required change falls outside allowedPaths, touches a forbidden path, or changes tool-discovery-scan@v1 semantics.
The UI would need to show a numeric remote fact, an enabled authorization or recharge action, or a deployed-compatibility claim without verified production contract evidence.
The future server specification would be presented as current deployed behavior or require modifying NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, or production configuration.
